archive_note: Per-source raw evidence remains historical; vendor_profiles provide the canonical version-scoped vendor evidence fields. Detailed product mechanisms and implementation designs belong to linked specialized docs. No vendor capability row is a test result for the target self-developed GPU.

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: Compute Sanitizer release notes 2026.3; NVCC online documentation CUDA Toolkit 13.4; compiler memcheck introduced with CUDA 13.1
hardware_requirements: Compatible NVIDIA CUDA device and matching CUDA Toolkit / Compute Sanitizer versions
Instruction and architecture coverage depends on device capabilities and exact tool release; do not assume all older SMs are supported
instrumentation: Default memcheck uses runtime binary instrumentation
Compile-time memcheck optionally performs original-object base-and-bounds analysis; unknown provenance falls back to current-allocation bounds
runtime_requirements: Use the corresponding Compute Sanitizer memcheck runtime for compiler-instrumented modules
Device modules/JIT/hybrid coverage and launch/resource bookkeeping must be checked against the selected toolkit version
detector_scope: memcheck global/local/shared device memory and supported allocation diagnostics
initcheck default global; shared/all selectable in documented versions
racecheck shared-memory data hazards, and synccheck supported synchronization misuse
known_limitations: Only memcheck is documented for compile-time instrumentation; other checker types are separate
Same-module function-level hybrid coverage cannot be assumed; supported granularity must be verified
Runtime-mode/current-address checks do not guarantee detection when an A-derived pointer lands in a distinct live B
No comprehensive device global/cross-kernel race checker is implied by racecheck

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: ROCm LLVM GPU ASan documentation docs-7.2.4; LLNL 7.0.0 examples and 7.13.0 preview are separate evidence, not equivalent baselines
hardware_requirements: Official documented GPU ASan deployment requires supported xnack+ GPU configuration and Linux HMM
Illustrative gfx90a:xnack+ offload architecture is not a universal target GPU setting
instrumentation: LLVM/Clang device memory instrumentation with GPU-visible Shadow/Poison/Redzone metadata
Software Shadow checks use GPU instructions; absence of a special Shadow ISA instruction does not invalidate an independently implemented checker
runtime_requirements: -fsanitize=address -shared-libsan with version-matched ASan-enabled HIP/HSA runtime libraries
HSA_XNACK=1 applies only where hardware and kernel support retryable faults; validate real device reports
detector_scope: Supported GPU device addressability and memory-error reports for instrumented accesses
Lifetime/poison checks within published Shadow state and officially supported memory spaces
known_limitations: xnack- offload targets may produce runnable but uninstrumented device code
Private/stack accesses are not generally instrumented in the cited implementation; LDS may be modeled as global
Finite Redzones and missing/uninitialized Shadow mapping can create missed detections or tool faults
XNACK fault retry does not automatically allocate valid Poison metadata for arbitrary wild pointers

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: Intel DPC++/C++ compiler 2026.0 documentation; independent Unified Runtime specification not assumed to share identical implementation status
hardware_requirements: Official 2026.0 GPU configuration documents Linux with one Intel Ponte Vecchio GPU card
Level Zero GPU device selection and SYCL versus OpenMP runtime setup must follow their distinct instructions
instrumentation: Unified Runtime / device backend collaborates on allocations and diagnostic metadata
runtime_requirements: SYCL Level Zero device selection or OpenMP unified_runtime plugin plus appropriate UR_ENABLE_LAYERS
Compatible Intel compiler / Unified Runtime / driver / GPU configuration
detector_scope: ASan supports documented global/USM/local/private memory errors and SYCL-specific buffer/context/free checks
MSan device uninitialized-use checks; TSan documented device USM race detection
known_limitations: Device ASan forces kernel execution into sequential mode, changing concurrency semantics
Large workgroup counts may lead to skipped ASan local/private and MSan local/private checks
Device private-memory overhead may reduce permitted workgroup size
Generic UR specification status for MSan/TSan cannot be treated as universal backend support

vendor_profiles.version_baseline: MUSA published v1.1.1 guide/release note; undated portions not assigned an invented release date
hardware_requirements: Follow explicit version-specific MUSA and driver hardware support tables; do not generalize an MTT S5000 example to all devices
instrumentation: Public documentation describes a GPU runtime debugging tool; internal machine-code/Shadow/provenance algorithm remains undisclosed
runtime_requirements: Matching mt-compute-sanitizer and supported MUSA runtime/driver environment
detector_scope: Publicly documented device global out-of-bounds and API-return-error checks
Memory leak detection requires the separately enabled leak-check mode
known_limitations: Current published descriptions do not establish complete private/shared/local/host-pinned coverage
Some atomic/special LSU paths are not established as supported in the cited guide
No evidence establishes equivalence to NV-R binary rewriting, AMD-B2 Shadow or NV-C original-object analysis
